examples.trans: Did you hear about this yesterday?
I was busy today because of yesterday.

meanings.note: Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.
I'll go first.

meanings.en: to be sorry; to feel apologetic
meanings.note: Descriptive adjective; used with peers or younger people (whereas 죄송하다 is honorific/humble).

examples.trans: I'm really sorry I'm late.

examples.text: 미안하지만 다시 한 번 말씀해 주세요.
examples.trans: I'm sorry, but please say that one more time.
I'm on my way home right now.
On weekends I usually rest at home.

meanings.note: Short for 문자 메시지.

examples.trans: I sent a text message.
Why aren't you replying to my text?

보다.gloss: to see, to watch; to take (an exam)

meanings.en: to see, to look at, to watch
meanings.note: Primary meaning.
Idiomatic in 시험을 보다.

examples.trans: I watched a movie on the weekend.
I took the driver's license exam.
I understand well (quickly, right away).
Today is a (quickly, right away) busy day.
Please come into the room.

examples.text: 올해 우리 회사에 신입사원이 많이 들어왔어요.
examples.trans: Many new employees joined our company this year.

meanings.note: Compound of 들다 (enter) + 오다 (come)

meanings.en: to join (a company, school, or group)

examples.trans: Come on, nice to meet you!
Come on, I understand now.
Did you hear about this gap, room?
I was busy today because of gap, room.

meanings.note: Placed directly before a noun in questions

examples.trans: What kind of music are you listening to right now?
Is something the matter?
I want to wait right now.
How about trying to wait together tomorrow?

meanings.note: Auxiliary verb used after -지 to tell someone not to do something. Ending with -고 (말고) gives a brisk, trailing command. RR: malda.

examples.trans: Please do not worry.
Do not be late, and come early.

meanings.note: Softens a statement or downplays a motive.

examples.trans: I just asked out of curiosity.
I'll just stay home today.

meanings.note: adverbial form of 빠르다 (to be fast)

examples.trans: Please get ready quickly.
Time goes by so fast.
I want to went inside right now.
How about trying to went inside together tomorrow?

meanings.note: interrogative pronoun; becomes 누가 before subject particle -가
indefinite pronoun

examples.trans: Did someone come outside?
Who is that person?

meanings.note: Interrogative adverb.

examples.trans: Why are you running?
Why were you late today?
Did you hear about this doorbell?
I was busy today because of doorbell.
I want to ring, press? right now.
How about trying to ring, press? together tomorrow?
Did you hear about this sweet filled pancakes?
I was busy today because of sweet filled pancakes.

meanings.note: Past tense is 샀다 / 샀어요.

examples.trans: I bought fruit at the mart.
I need to buy a birthday present for my friend.

meanings.en: to come (of a feeling, state, or weather)
meanings.note: Used in expressions like 혼란이 오다 (confusion comes) or 비가 오다 (rain falls)

examples.text: 한국에 온 지 일 년 됐어요.
examples.trans: It's been one year since I came to Korea.
I suddenly started feeling sleepy.
Did you hear about this green tea?
I was busy today because of green tea.
There are five here.
Altogether, it is five people.

meanings.note: General-purpose counter noun used with native Korean determiners (한 개, 두 개, 세 개).

examples.trans: How many do you need?
I bought three loaves of bread.

meanings.note: Someone who started earlier than you.

examples.trans: school senior
My senior bought me a meal.

meanings.note: Often used directly without a locative particle to mean 'here'.

examples.trans: Please sit here.
Here is our office.

meanings.note: Casual exclamation used to call someone younger or a close friend.

examples.trans: Hey, come quickly!
Hey, where are you going?
Do you have time today?
Where are you going?

meanings.note: Used only with close friends, younger people, or children
colloquial contraction of 무엇; also used rhetorically to brush off a question

examples.trans: What are you doing now?
Why are you even asking something like that?

meanings.en: to do, to perform, to hold
meanings.note: Core verb; also combines with nouns to form verbs.

examples.trans: What are you doing right now?
We are holding a meeting today.

meanings.note: Used for time or order.

examples.trans: Let's meet next time.
The next station is Seoul Station.

meanings.note: Used when repeating an action.

examples.trans: See you again!
It is raining again.

meanings.note: Action of coming together with someone.

examples.trans: I meet a friend.
Let's meet tomorrow.
